This morning she noticed that neck flexion causes an electric shock-like sensation that shoots into her left arm and left leg, prompting her husband to bring her to the emergency department. She also describes unexplained fatigue disproportionate to her activity level for the past 6-8 months, and she noticed that her walking became noticeably worse after jogging or after a hot shower during the current episode. She denies visual loss, eye pain, diplopia, facial numbness, difficulty swallowing, hearing changes, bladder or bowel incontinence, fever, weight loss, joint pain, skin rashes, oral ulcers, dry eyes, or dry mouth. She has no history of seizures or head trauma. There is no family history of neurological disease.

results.title: Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: 2017 revisions of the McDonald criteria
results.authors: Thompson AJ, Banwell BL, Barkhof F, et al.
results.key_findings: Under the 2017 revision, CSF-specific oligoclonal bands (present in CSF but absent from matched serum) can substitute for MRI-based dissemination in time (DIT) when dissemination in space (DIS) is already established. Symptomatic MRI lesions may now be used toward DIS. Cortical lesions are accepted alongside juxtacortical lesions for DIS.

results.title: MRI criteria for the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: MAGNIMS consensus guidelines
results.authors: Filippi M, Rocca MA, Ciccarelli O, et al.
results.key_findings: DIS requires at least one T2 lesion in at least 2 of 4 CNS regions: periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal cord. Three or more periventricular lesions are required to meet the periventricular criterion.

results.title: Multiple sclerosis
results.authors: Reich DS, Lucchinetti CF, Calabresi PA.
results.key_findings: RRMS accounts for approximately 85% of MS cases at onset. Disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) range from platform agents (interferons, glatiramer, teriflunomide, dimethyl fumarate) to high-efficacy agents (natalizumab, ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, cladribine, S1P modulators). NEDA-3 (no relapses, no disability progression, no new MRI lesions) is a treatment target.

output.summary: The 2017 McDonald criteria require demonstration of dissemination in space (DIS) and dissemination in time (DIT) for an MS diagnosis. DIS is met by T2 lesions in at least 2 of 4 characteristic locations (periventricular, juxtacortical/cortical, infratentorial, spinal cord). DIT is demonstrated by simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on a single MRI, a new T2 or gadolinium-enhancing lesion on follow-up imaging, or — importantly under the 2017 revision — by the presence of CSF-specific oligoclonal bands. Choice of DMT should balance efficacy, safety profile, and patient factors including reproductive plans and comorbidities.

output.proposed: Natalizumab 300 mg IV every 4 weeks (or alternative first/high-efficacy DMT for RRMS)
interactions: Oral contraceptive (ethinylestradiol/norgestimate): No pharmacokinetic interaction with natalizumab or dimethyl fumarate. Note that teriflunomide does not significantly interact with oral contraceptives, but patients should be counseled if switching DMTs that affect hepatic metabolism.
contraindications: Natalizumab: contraindicated in patients with active infection or prior PML; JC virus (JCV) antibody positivity at high index (>1.5) with prior IS use significantly increases PML risk — risk stratification required
Cladribine and ofatumumab: not recommended in pregnancy or breastfeeding; effective contraception required
Teriflunomide: contraindicated in pregnancy (teratogenic, Pregnancy Category X); requires accelerated elimination procedure if pregnancy occurs
warnings: Check JC virus antibody index before initiating natalizumab; repeat every 6 months in JCV-positive patients
Screen for hepatitis B and C before initiating ocrelizumab or ofatumumab
Live-attenuated vaccines must be completed at least 4-6 weeks before initiating immunosuppressive DMTs; contraindicated after B-cell depletion or S1P modulator initiation
Fingolimod and other S1P modulators require baseline ECG and first-dose cardiac monitoring for bradyarrhythmia; avoid in patients with prior MI, second-degree AV block, or sick sinus syndrome
Dimethyl fumarate: monitor CBC at baseline, 6 months, and annually — risk of prolonged lymphopenia; withhold if lymphocytes <500 cells/microL for >6 months (PML risk)
Oral contraceptive and dimethyl fumarate: no clinically significant interaction identified
Penicillin allergy does not affect DMT selection for MS

results.title: International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders
results.authors: Wingerchuk DM, Banwell B, Bennett JL, et al.
results.key_findings: NMOSD core clinical criteria include optic neuritis, acute myelitis, area postrema syndrome (nausea/hiccups), brainstem syndrome, diencephalic syndrome, and cerebral syndrome. AQP4-IgG seropositive NMOSD requires one core clinical feature. Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (spanning ≥3 vertebral segments) is a hallmark MRI finding. Short-segment cord lesions (<3 segments) and periventricular Dawson fingers are more consistent with MS.

results.title: Diagnosis of MOG antibody-associated disease: International MOGAD Panel proposed criteria
results.key_findings: MOGAD is characterised by MOG-IgG positivity by cell-based assay, with core presentations including optic neuritis (often bilateral), myelitis, ADEM-like phenotype, and cortical encephalitis. Cerebellar involvement can occur. MRI lesions in MOGAD often partially or fully resolve, unlike MS. Thalamic and cortical lesions favour MOGAD over MS.

output.summary: NMOSD is distinguished from MS by AQP4-IgG seropositivity, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, area postrema involvement, and the absence of classic periventricular Dawson fingers on MRI. MOGAD requires MOG-IgG positivity by cell-based assay and typically presents with optic neuritis, myelitis, or ADEM-like syndromes; lesions often show more complete resolution than MS. Both require exclusion (negative AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG by cell-based assay) before a confident MS diagnosis. Short-segment spinal cord lesions, periventricular lesions in Dawson fingers configuration, and CSF oligoclonal bands in the absence of AQP4-IgG or MOG-IgG support MS.

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no role in MS diagnosis — findings are non-specific and do not contribute to dissemination in space or time criteria.
CT is markedly inferior to MRI for visualizing demyelinating plaques and adds radiation exposure without diagnostic benefit in this context.
No cardiac indication; echocardiography does not inform the demyelinating differential and is not part of standard MS workup.
Cardiac monitoring is relevant only for first-dose fingolimod initiation — not as part of the MS diagnostic workup.
FDG-PET is not indicated for MS diagnosis or follow-up; it does not differentiate demyelinating from inflammatory or infectious etiologies and carries substantial cost.

sequence_constraints.reason: Standard pre-LP brain imaging: confirm absence of mass effect or signs of raised intracranial pressure before lumbar puncture

critical_actions: Establish dissemination in space (DIS) using brain and spinal-cord MRI in MS-typical regions (periventricular, juxtacortical/cortical, infratentorial, spinal cord)

Establish dissemination in time (DIT) by demonstrating simultaneous enhancing and non-enhancing lesions on MRI, or by CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands (per McDonald 2017) — the positive OCBs satisfy DIT in this case alongside established DIS
Exclude NMOSD and MOGAD with AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG cell-based assays before committing to an MS diagnosis and initiating DMT
Order CSF analysis with paired serum to assess oligoclonal bands and IgG index

Treat the acute relapse with high-dose IV methylprednisolone (1 g daily for 3-5 days) to hasten recovery from the cerebellar and sensory relapse; reserve plasma exchange for steroid-refractory severe relapses
Initiate a disease-modifying therapy (DMT) after relapse stabilization; in a woman of reproductive age, discuss teratogenicity profile of each agent and family planning goals before DMT selection
Check JC virus antibody serostatus before considering natalizumab; verify vaccination status (especially live-attenuated vaccines) prior to B-cell depleting or S1P modulator DMT initiation
Supplement vitamin D and counsel on heat avoidance (Uhthoff phenomenon), smoking cessation, and aerobic exercise as evidence-based modifiable factors in MS
contraindicated_actions: Do not diagnose MS on the basis of non-specific white matter lesions alone without meeting McDonald 2017 criteria (DIS + DIT) and excluding mimics

Do not interpret borderline-normal B12 (228 pg/mL, within reference range 200-900 pg/mL) as the cause of a multifocal CNS demyelinating syndrome — subacute combined degeneration does not produce gadolinium-enhancing periventricular lesions or CSF oligoclonal bands
Do not start natalizumab in a JC virus-antibody-positive patient (particularly with high index) without explicit PML risk-benefit discussion and shared decision-making
Do not initiate teriflunomide or cladribine without effective contraception and full teratogenicity counseling in a woman of reproductive age
Do not administer fingolimod or other S1P modulators without baseline ECG and mandated first-dose cardiac monitoring
Do not administer live-attenuated vaccines after initiating B-cell depleting therapy (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab) or S1P modulators
Do not use chronic oral corticosteroids as maintenance therapy for MS — ineffective and harmful long-term
key_reasoning_points: The 2017 McDonald criteria require DIS and DIT plus exclusion of better explanations — the positive CSF oligoclonal bands fulfill DIT when DIS is already established by MRI (periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal cord), so repeat MRI at a later date is not required for diagnosis in this case

The Lhermitte sign (electric shock radiating into the limbs on neck flexion) reflects posterior column or dorsal cervical cord irritation and is a characteristic, though not specific, feature of MS; it should prompt spinal cord imaging

Cerebellar/pontine relapse with gait ataxia, ipsilateral dysmetria, and gaze-evoked nystagmus localizes to the posterior fossa, consistent with the enhancing left middle cerebellar peduncle lesion — a classic infratentorial MS region

B12 at 228 pg/mL falls within the laboratory reference range (200-900 pg/mL) and does not explain gadolinium-enhancing periventricular T2 lesions or CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands — subacute combined degeneration is excluded as the primary diagnosis, and the B12 value is a carefully planted distractor

OCT demonstrating left RNFL thinning in a patient without a history of symptomatic optic neuritis indicates prior subclinical optic pathway demyelination — this finding provides evidence for dissemination in space independently of the presenting cerebellar relapse

AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG must both be obtained by cell-based assay (not ELISA), as older ELISA-based AQP4 tests carry unacceptable false-negative rates; negative results are required to exclude NMOSD and MOGAD before initiating MS-specific DMT

metadata.difficulty_description: Straightforward RRMS case presenting with left cerebellar relapse (ataxia, dysmetria) and left arm sensory symptoms, with prior episode attributed to cervical radiculopathy. MRI shows multifocal periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, and spinal cord T2 lesions with single enhancing lesion; CSF OCBs positive; AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG negative. McDonald 2017 criteria fully met. Red herring: borderline-normal B12 in the context of prior iron deficiency anemia.
metadata.mcdonald_criteria_met: 2017 McDonald criteria met: DIS (periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal cord — all 4 regions) and DIT (simultaneous enhancing left MCP and non-enhancing lesions on single MRI, plus CSF OCBs)
metadata.educational_value: Cerebellar relapse presentation (left MCP enhancing lesion) with subclinical optic pathway involvement on OCT/VEP; demonstrates use of CSF OCBs for DIT; B12 red herring tests discrimination of nutritional myelopathy from inflammatory demyelination
metadata.real_seed_note: A verified CC-BY 4.0 confirmed-RRMS case (PMC11699731, PMID 39674029, Clinics São Paulo) was retrieved during authoring but describes a clinically distinct patient (67-year-old Caucasian Brazilian woman with late-onset RRMS, brain-predominant lesions, no documented cord lesion). Because the present case body — demographics (32-year-old Hispanic woman), cerebellar relapse, spinal cord involvement, and enhancing-plus-non-enhancing MRI — does not derive from that patient, no PMID is asserted (per project policy, a PMID is cited only when the case body is genuinely seeded from it). This is an authentic, clinically plausible confirmed-RRMS case authored de novo by a neuroimmunology domain expert agent to match McDonald 2017 RRMS criteria, and is not extracted from any specific published patient.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Straightforward RRMS: 6 required tools, multifocal MRI in all 4 McDonald regions, CSF OCBs positive, AQP4/MOG negative. Single red herring (borderline B12). Diagnosis does not require cross-modality synthesis beyond standard MS workup.
